market: A hard risk-off session led by the unwinding AI trade: QQQ (the Nasdaq-100 ETF) is down 4.6%, SPY (the S&P 500 ETF) down 2.8%, and IWM (the small-cap ETF) down 2.2% at 1:29 PM CT, with the VIX near 33. The stories are a seventh straight fall in Nvidia, a weak first day for the Anthropic IPO, a 6% drop in Taiwan's market, and talk of a December Fed rate hike after hawkish minutes; the 10-year yield slipped to 4.94% as money moved to bonds and defensive sectors. Small caps are holding up better than large-cap tech because they own little of the AI trade, but levered and thin names are being sold hard. Stock-specific moves in small caps are mostly biotech FDA delays and retail earnings.

verdicts.name: FNKO
verdicts.thesis: Funko is down about 13.5% with no news, filing or press release behind it, on a day when the whole market is being sold and thin, indebted names are hit hardest. That looks more like a holder getting out in a bad tape than new information, so a partial rebound against IWM is the slightly better bet over the next few sessions. It is not a take because the cause is unknown, the credit lines are fully drawn with a refinancing needed, and heavy unexplained selling in a company in that position can be someone knowing about a financing.
verdicts.dilution: Cash $41.6M at Sept 30 against about $196M of debt; the $124.3M revolver is fully drawn and the $72.9M term loan pays down $4.1M a quarter, all at SOFR plus 4.5% and due Dec 31, 2027, so it turns current after Dec 31, 2026 unless refinanced. Leverage and fixed-charge covenants begin with the Dec 31, 2026 quarter; the company was in compliance at Sept 30 with no going-concern language. The 10-Q mentions an S-3 shelf and a Sales Agreement (a possible at-the-market share program) without details the research could confirm; no convertibles, warrants or open share sale were found, but the last part of the 10-Q was not read.
verdicts.company: Funko Inc. Class A Common Stock
verdicts.why: No earnings report, but a large move on heavy volume. -13.1% so far today (-10.9% against IWM, the small-cap ETF, which did -2.2%), 1.6 typical daily ranges, on 2.2 times usual volume (projected to a full day); opened -1.8% from the last close; last 5.85
